title: Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan Transfers and Activity on the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account
content:
Holding a Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan changes when a Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account is inactive.

- An early wage transfer delivered to the card is a load and therefore activity, exactly like a payroll load. A cardholder who receives early pay on the card is not inactive for the inactivity period that follows it.
- A card autorecovery debit taken for the Access plan under the cardholder's standing authorization is not cardholder-initiated and is never activity.
- The same early wage transfer never starts a new card pay period for the free withdrawal and free card-to-bank allowances, which reset only on a payroll load.

| Entry on the card | Counts as activity | Starts a new card pay period |
|---|---|---|
| payroll load | yes | yes |
| early wage transfer delivered to the card | yes | no |
| card autorecovery debit for the Access plan | no | no |

*Hypothetical case:* the last payroll load posted 120 days ago on a plan with a 90-day inactivity period, and an early wage transfer reached the card 30 days ago. The account is not inactive, because the transfer is its last activity. The pay period that began with the payroll load continues, so the free withdrawals already used in it stay used.
